news.title: 53,800-seater World Cup stadium labelled unfit for purpose and may be demolished
news.lede: A FORMER World Cup stadium has been branded no longer fit for purpose just 21 years after its last renovation. The Waldstadion has been the home of Bundesliga side Eintracht Frankfurt since 1925. It’s undergone several renovations over the years, with the most recent being completed in 2005 ahead of the Fifa Confederations Cup and World Cup the following summer. That transformed the Waldstadion, which is known as Deutsche Bank Park for sponsorship reasons, into a football-only stadium.

news.title: FIFA's wealth comes from astronomical ticket prices at the World Cup and revenue of as much as five billion dollars
news.lede: FIFA earned five billion dollars from ticket sales for the 2026 World Cup. The 2026 World Cup brought in more money than expected for FIFA. The Times reported that the world football body has raised $5 billion from ticket sales, more than five times the $929 million it raised from the Qatar World Cup. FIFA's plan was for $3,3 billion from ticket sales, but it was greatly exceeded, with total revenue from the 2026 World Cup estimated at around $15 billion.

news.title: FIFA confirm staggering World Cup revenue after controversial ticket policy
news.lede: FIFA are thought to have earned a staggering £3.8billion in ticket and hospitality sales from the World Cup this summer - five times more than they did at the tournament in Qatar four years ago. The World Cup in North America was the first to have 104 matches as FIFA increased the amount of nations who qualified and introduced an extra knockout round. The increased amount of games, 40 more than there were in 2022, has allowed football's governing body to benefit financially with record fees generated. The Times has reported that the aforementioned figure, which was not confirmed by the organisation, far exceeded what FIFA anticipated to earn and contributed to its overall World Cup revenue of $15bn (£11.27bn).

news.title: Morocco vs North Korea: How & When to Watch the U17 Women's World Cup Round of 16 Clash
news.lede: Rabat – Morocco’s U17 Women’s national team return to action today, Wednesday, October 28, as they take on heavyweights North Korea in a high-stakes Round of 16 clash at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Maâmora. Youness Rabie’s side enter the knockout phase determined to write a new chapter in Moroccan women's football history. Having reached the Round of 16 as one of the best third-placed teams, the host nation faces a familiar roadblock: the very same North Korean side that ended their tournament run at this exact stage last year before going on to lift the trophy. North Korea arrive in Maâmora as four-time world champions in this age category and clear tournament favorites.

news.title: Gianni Infantino critic quits over World Cup controversy in latest Fifa re-election twist
news.lede: Japan Football Association vice-president Takeshi Okada has stepped down from his role over controversies surrounding this year's Fifa World Cup. Okada's departure occurred just one week after the Asian Football Confederation officially endorsed Fifa president Gianni Infantino for re-election. The former Japan manager stated that recent governance actions surrounding the tournament significantly diverged from his personal convictions regarding sporting integrity. The resignation highlights internal divisions within the Asian football governing body despite its recent public show of support for Infantino.

news.title: Telford football referee returns from 'incredible' China tournament
news.lede: A young football referee who has just returned from officiating at a world schools tournament in China has said it was a "scary" but also "incredible" experience. Callum Oram, 18, has been refereeing for three years and hopes to make it his full time career. He spent 11 days working at the International School Sport Federation Football World Cup in Suzhou and made friends with other young referees from around the world. The Telford College student said he believed the tournament would be a valuable learning experience and would help him move ahead in the game.
